The sequence is geometric with first term $729 = 3^6$ and ratio $r = 3^{-2}$, so $a_k = 3^{8-2k}$.
$P_n = 3^{\sum_{k=1}^{n}(8-2k)} = 3^{8n-n(n+1)} = 3^{7n-n^2}$
$(P_n)^{1/n} = 3^{7-n}$
$\sum_{n=1}^{40} 3^{7-n} = 3^6+3^5+\dots+3^{-33}$, which is a geometric progression with ratio $\frac13$ and 40 terms.
Sum $= \dfrac{3^6(1-3^{-40})}{1-\frac13} = \dfrac{3^7(1-3^{-40})}{2}$
$2\sum_{n=1}^{40} (P_n)^{1/n} = 3^7 - 3^{-33} = \dfrac{3^{40}-1}{3^{33}}$
Comparing with $\dfrac{3^\alpha-1}{3^\beta}$ gives $\alpha = 40$ and $\beta = 33$, with $\gcd(40,33) = 1$.
$\alpha+\beta = 73$
Answer: (A) 73
